storm.summary_layperson: No storm risk this evening: radar is clear, there are no weather alerts, and the cove gets the same quiet, chilly, breezy night as the surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer in play: the Sound (57°F) is about 18°F warmer than the air at 4 PM and the gap widens to roughly 19–20°F by 7 PM as the air cools — but there is nothing inbound for it to matter.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: yesterday's coastal low has moved away and a cool, dry north wind has filled in behind it across the whole region. KOKX radar shows no rain or storm cells anywhere in the approach to the cove, and there are no NWS watches, warnings or advisories. The NWS carried a slight chance of light rain only until about 4 PM; that window has closed with no rain recorded at Riverside YC.

Why the risk is low: instability is zero (CAPE 0 J/kg), so there is no energy available for thunderstorms. Winds aloft are moderately strong (shear about 26 kt, rising to the low 30s this evening), but shear without instability or a trigger produces nothing. Pressure is steady near 1004 hPa and every station around the Sound agrees on a north to north-northwest wind, with no sign of a boundary or front moving through.

Local modifier — none tonight: the Sound protects the cove in summer, when its water is much colder than the air and a stable layer of cool air sits over it. In mid-November it is the reverse: the water is 57°F and the air is about 39–41°F, so the water is roughly 18°F warmer than the air. That gap only grows through the evening (about 19–20°F by 7 PM) as the air keeps cooling while the Sound holds its temperature. Sunset is at 4:37 PM and there is no sea breeze. Nothing local would weaken or strengthen incoming weather — and tonight there is none to act on.

Most likely outcome: a dry, cloudy, cold evening with a gusty north-northwest breeze easing after dark. Temperatures slip from about 41°F to the upper 30s. The cove sees the same weather as Stamford, Rye and Port Chester.

What would change the call: new showers appearing on radar to the north or northwest, or an NWS alert. Neither is hinted at in the current data.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient wind from the north-northwest — no sea breeze
wind.tactics_blurb: Offshore north-northwest wind coming over the land: puffy and shifty, with the best average pressure in the middle of the cove away from the shoreline lees. Stay center, tack on the headers, and expect the breeze to ease after dark and back left toward northwest late.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: a moderate gradient wind day — no sea breeze in play. The wind is the large-scale flow behind yesterday's departed coastal low, not anything thermal. Well-sited airport and buoy anemometers average about 10 kt, and 89% of the 28 stations around the Sound agree on a north to north-northwest direction. A sea breeze is impossible tonight: it needs land warmer than the water, and the air is about 18°F colder than the 57°F Sound (air–water temperature difference of −18°F), with sunset at 4:37 PM before the window even opens.

Right now at Riverside YC: north to north-northwest, 10-minute average 11 kt, gusting 15–16 kt, with the instantaneous direction swinging between about 340° and 010° in a few minutes. The Western Sound buoy shows more in open water: NNW 13 kt gusting 20.

Through the window: because this is gradient wind, it does not die at sunset. It does ease as the air near the ground settles after dark: about 10 kt at 5 PM, 8 kt by 7 PM, and a soft spot near 6 kt around 8 PM, before a small recovery to about 7 kt. Direction holds north-northwest (around 340°) until about 8 PM, then backs left toward northwest (about 320°) by 9 PM — a one-way shift, not an oscillation, so late in the window the left side of a beat gains.

Where the pressure is: a north-northwest wind reaches the cove over land, trees and houses, so it arrives in puffs with holes between them — typical swings of 15–30° that reward tacking on headers. The best average breeze is usually mid-cove, away from the immediate lee of the northern and western shores. That is why the call is to stay center rather than bank on either side.

What it feels like: 8–10 kt with puffs to the mid-teens is good dinghy breeze early in the window, dropping toward light-air sailing (6–7 kt, puffs near 10) after 8 PM. It is cold — about 41°F falling to the upper 30s — and fully dark for the whole window.

Model versus observations: the HRRR model agrees with the stations on direction (343° forecast versus 342° observed) but is running about 3 kt under what Riverside YC is measuring, so the speeds here are nudged up from the model in the early hours. The model run available at publish time reached only to 9 PM; the 10 PM row carries the 9 PM values forward.

data_caveats: HRRR 20Z run had only posted through 9 PM at publish time — the 10 PM wind row is carried forward from 9 PM, not modeled
HRRR is running about 3 kt below Riverside YC's measured wind — early-window speeds are nudged up toward the observations
Gust values are estimated from Riverside YC's current gust-to-average ratio (no model gust field)
NWS forecast text covers 'This Afternoon' only (chance of light rain before 4 PM) — the sky label may overstate rain chances for the evening
